s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging, asymptomatic, reddish-brown skin lesion with peripheral ecchymosis
salient_findings: Reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis
Vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40
key_facts: 5-year history of lesion
Spontaneous onset with no previous trauma
No improvement with topical antifungal cream
No local lymphadenopathy
Negative for HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C
Ki-67 index showed low proliferation in endothelial cells
Poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation
Prominent hemosiderin deposits on Perls Prussian blue staining

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: reddish-brown skin lesion with peripheral ecchymosis and vascular proliferation

shortlist.label: granuloma faciale
shortlist.why_kept: asymptomatic, reddish-brown skin lesion with peripheral ecchymosis

shortlist.label: erythema elevatum diutinum
shortlist.why_kept: asymptomatic, reddish-brown skin lesion with peripheral ecchymosis

shortlist.label: cutaneous lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: gradually enlarging skin lesion with negative serologic tests

shortlist.label: angioma
shortlist.why_kept: vascular proliferation and prominent hemosiderin deposits

raw.rationale: The presence of a reddish hematomalike plaque, poorly defined dermal vascular proliferation, and prominent hemosiderin deposits are consistent with Kaposi's sarcoma, especially given the negative serologic tests for HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C, which rules out some other causes but still leaves Kaposi's as a possibility due to its characteristic histological features.

rejected.label: granuloma faciale
rejected.why: Typically presents with brownish plaques on the face, not matching the axillary location in this case

rejected.label: erythema elevatum diutinum
rejected.why: Characterized by tender, red-brown plaques often on the extensor surfaces, which doesn't fit the asymptomatic nature and location of the lesion

rejected.label: cutaneous lymphoma
rejected.why: Would likely show more significant cellular pleomorphism and a higher Ki-67 index, not consistent with the low proliferation rate in endothelial cells observed here

rejected.label: angioma
rejected.why: While it could present with vascular proliferation, the specific combination of clinical and histological features, including the presence of hemosiderin deposits and the characteristic vascular channel morphology, points more towards Kaposi's sarcoma
